drivingQuestion: How do we know the kosher fish was swallowed rather than spawned?
outcomeNote: difficulty answered by three case-limitations and Rav Ashi's majority rule

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ טַעְמָא דַּחֲזֵינֵיהּ דִּבְלַע, הָא לָא חֲזֵינֵיהּ דִּבְלַע — אָמְרִי: אַשְׁרוֹצֵי אַשְׁרֵיץ.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara infers from the language of the mishna: In the case of a non-kosher fish that swallowed a kosher fish: «The reason» consumption of the kosher fish is permitted is «that we saw that» the non-kosher fish «swallowed» the kosher fish. «But» if «we did not see it swallow» the kosher fish «we say» that perhaps the non-kosher fish «spawned» the kosher fish, and it is forbidden.

segments.he: מְנָלַן? דְּתַנְיָא: דָּג טָמֵא מַשְׁרִיץ, דָּג טָהוֹר מֵטִיל בֵּיצִים. אִי הָכִי, כִּי חָזֵינָא דִּבְלַע אָמְרִינַן: הַאי אִיעַכַּלָא, וְהַאי אַשְׁרוֹצֵי אַשְׁרֵיץ!
segments.en: «From where do we» derive that we must have this concern? «As it is taught» in a baraita: «A non-kosher fish spawns» offspring, while «a kosher fish lays eggs» from which the offspring hatch. The Gemara challenges: «If so,» even «when we saw it swallowing» a kosher fish «we» should «say» that «that» fish that it swallowed «was digested, and this» one, which was found inside of the non-kosher fish, it «spawned,» and should be forbidden.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: כְּגוֹן שֶׁמְּצָאוֹ דֶּרֶךְ הָרֶיעִי. רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁמְּצָאוֹ דֶּרֶךְ בֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה. רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁמְּצָאוֹ שָׁלֵם.
segments.en: «Rav Sheshet says:» It is referring to a case «where» one «found» the kosher fish in «the digestive tract,» which is not where the non-kosher fish normally spawns its offspring. «Rav Pappa says» similarly: It is referring to a case «where» one «found» the kosher fish in «the passageway of the gullet. Rav Naḥman says:» It is referring to a case «where» one «found it whole» and in complete form, and not as a newly hatched fish.

segments.he: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: רוֹב דָּגִים בְּמִינָן מַשְׁרִיצִין, וּכְמִי שֶׁבָּלַע לְפָנֵינוּ דָּמֵי.
segments.en: «Rav Ashi says:» Do not infer from the mishna that it is referring to a case where the non-kosher fish was seen swallowing the kosher fish. Rather, the reason it is permitted to consume the swallowed fish is that «the majority of fish spawn» offspring «of their» own «species, and» therefore the case of a kosher fish discovered inside a non-kosher fish «is considered as if» the non-kosher fish had «swallowed» the kosher fish «in our presence.»
